title: Moonshot Mission Control
description: Device certificates and topic policies identify publishers. Consumers need timestamps, schema checks and event IDs; neither stream partitioning nor a diagram establishes global event order. Cross-account Firehose delivery needs an execution role, destination bucket policy and KMS permissions. Research access uses scoped roles, approved datasets, workgroups and protected query-result storage; not all these resources are expanded. Protected audit retention assumes S3 versioning, configured Object Lock and appropriately restricted administrators. The organization trail captures applicable AWS API activity, not every sensor payload. Cognito represents federated application sign-in; a backend credential broker or approved federation path must map researchers to scoped AWS query roles. No Cognito-to-Athena direct API call is implied by the identity line. This system is fictional and has no flight-control authority.

edges.meaning: Device certificates and IoT policies bind each device to allowed telemetry topics.
An IoT rule forwards validated topic traffic using an ingestion role.
Event-source mapping consumes batches; late and duplicate records require event IDs and timestamps.
Processor publishes custom metrics; configured alarms evaluate the metrics.
Alarm transitions notify operators; no flight-control action is implied.
Independent archival consumer buffers delivery without blocking live alarms.
Cross-account S3 writes require delivery-role, bucket and KMS key policies.
KMS key policy authorizes encryption and separately scoped decryption; this is key association.
Federated analysts assume constrained research roles; arbitrary lake access is not granted.
Queries use approved datasets and restricted results storage; workgroup and result bucket are omitted.
Organization trail captures applicable AWS API activity, not every telemetry payload.
Audit retention assumes configured Object Lock, versioning and constrained deletion privileges.
